newsitem.title: GABON: Gabon calls parliamentary elections for Sunday.
newsitem.headline: Gabon calls parliamentary elections for Sunday.

text.p: Gabon has announced that it will hold the first round of its much-delayed parliamentary elections on Sunday, with a second round on December 29.
A government spokesman announced the new dates after a cabinet meeting in the Central African nation on Monday.
The head of the electoral commission, citing organisational problems, postponed the election indefinitely on November 30, less than 24 hours before voters were to go to the polls.
At the time, Nguema Essono cited problems stemming from chaotic local elections on October 20, in particular names disappearing from voter lists.
Gabon, an oil-producing former French colony of 1.2 million people, has an electorate of about 479,000.

Sunday's vote will be Gabon's second multiparty legislative polls. The first were in 1990 when a wave of democratic reform swept across Africa after the fall of Communism in the Soviet Union and Eastern Europe.
The elections are part of a timetable of democratic and electoral reforms brokered in Paris after violence marred President Omar Bongo's 1993 relection.
More than 1,000 candidates will bid for 120 seats in the national assembly on Sunday.

Bongo's Democratic Party is expected to face strong competition from the Woodcutter's Party, led by Roman Catholic priest Father Paul Mba Abessole, which won the capital Libreville during the municipal polls.
Bongo has ruled the former French colony since 1968 after the death of Gabon's founding head of state, Leon Mba.
